summary: This note describes delta atracotoxin (δ-ACTX-Ar1, also called robustoxin), a 42-residue neurotoxic peptide in the venom of the Sydney funnel-web spider (Atrax robustus). It covers the toxin's structure, including its cystine knot and three charged surface patches, and its mechanism of slowing sodium channel inactivation in primates and affecting potassium and calcium channels in insects. The note also covers venom toxicity, envenomation symptoms, and the development of funnel-web spider antivenom.
one_line: Delta atracotoxin is a 42-residue neurotoxic peptide from Sydney funnel-web spider venom that disrupts sodium channel inactivation.
key_facts: Delta atracotoxin (δ-ACTX-Ar1, robustoxin, or robustotoxin) is a low-molecular-weight neurotoxic polypeptide found in the venom of the Sydney funnel-web spider (Atrax robustus).
Delta atracotoxin is a 42-residue peptide toxin with the chemical formula C206H313N59O59S9.
The amino acid sequence of delta atracotoxin contains three consecutive cysteine residues at positions 14–16.
The structure consists of a small triple-stranded beta-sheet stabilized by a disulfide knot, followed by a C-terminal extension comprising three classic or inverse y-turns.
Delta atracotoxin produces potentially fatal neurotoxic symptoms in primates by slowing the inactivation of sodium ion channels in autonomic and motor neurons.
In the spiders' intended insect prey, delta atracotoxin exerts its activity upon potassium and calcium ion channels.

Since 1927, records have been kept of envenomations of humans by the Sydney funnel-web spider, and 14 deaths were reported in medical literature between 1927 and 1981, when the antivenom became available.
In all cases in which the sex of the spider was determined, death occurred after a bite from a male spider.
The male funnel-web spider's venom appears to be six times more powerful than the female's, based on minimum lethal dose determinations.
The LD50 of pure delta atracotoxin isolated from a male spider was 0.15 mg/kg body weight in mice, compared with 3.3 mg/kg for male spider venom and 50 mg/kg for female spider venom.
Delta atracotoxin acts by voltage-dependent binding to neurotoxin receptor site-3, in a similar but not identical fashion to scorpion alpha-toxins and sea anemone toxins.
Under voltage-clamp conditions in dorsal root ganglion neurons, the synthetic toxin's effects on sodium currents were not significantly different from those of the native toxin.
Neither native nor synthetic d-ACTX-Ar1a had any effect on TTX-resistant sodium currents, but both selectively modulated TTX-sensitive sodium currents.
Symptoms in primates began with respiratory disturbances in the first 25 minutes, and severe hypotension occurred after 40–100 minutes.
The antivenom was developed by a team headed by Struan Sutherland at the Commonwealth Serum Laboratories in Melbourne.

Funnel web spider antivenom is prepared from the plasma of rabbits immunized with the venom of the male funnel web spider, and each vial contains 125 units standardized to neutralize 1.25 mg of venom.
